denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 19318 (bilateral reduction mammaplasty) with date of service 2026-02-25. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation submitted does not establish failure of conservative therapy or an expected resection weight meeting the policy threshold.

criteria.text: Symptoms attributable to macromastia documented for at least 6 months, such as neck, shoulder, or upper back pain, shoulder grooving, or inframammary intertrigo.
At least 3 months of conservative treatment, including a supportive garment plus physical therapy, analgesics, or dermatologic treatment of intertrigo, without adequate relief.
Estimated resection weight per breast at or above the 22nd percentile of the Schnur sliding scale for the patient's body surface area.
Photographic documentation of macromastia and shoulder grooving.

chart.text: A1c came back 6.4. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

55 year old woman here about her breasts, referred by her primary. Exam: large pendulous breasts, nipple to notch 32 on the right and 33 on the left, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both inframammary folds. Discussed reduction, risks, scars, sensation, the works. Her history otherwise: hypertension on lisinopril. Surgeries: a C-section. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works as a nurse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. She has had the neck and upper back pain for 20 months now, maybe longer, says it is daily by the afternoon. The bra straps have worn grooves into both shoulders and she gets the rash under the breasts every summer. She has been in a fitted supportive bra from the specialty shop for months, takes ibuprofen most days, treats the rash with nystatin powder. I am sending her to PT for posture and scapular work. She is 5 foot 4, 228 pounds, which puts BSA right around 2.16. Schnur 22nd percentile at that BSA is about 838 grams. I am estimating 1098 grams on the right and 1048 on the left.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Eval for upper back and neck pain in the setting of large breasts. Forward shoulder posture, tight pecs, weak lower traps. Plan 8 weeks, twice a week, scapular stabilization and postural retraining.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports slight improvement that does not last.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Session 6. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.

Back to go over the plan. Symptoms unchanged. We went through the operation again and she wants to proceed if insurance will cover it. Vitals today 131 over 71, pulse 85. Finished 8 weeks of PT across the street, says it helped while she was there and then right back to baseline. Still in the supportive bra, still on the ibuprofen, intertrigo treated with nystatin powder with partial relief. That is 5 months of conservative measures without durable relief.
Standard pre-op photo series taken today, front, both obliques, both laterals. Grooving visible at both shoulders in the AP view, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both folds.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 223, LDL 147, HDL 55, triglycerides 161. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Pre-op visit. Consent signed, marked the plan on her in the mirror, superomedial pedicle, Wise pattern. Labs fine. Stop the ibuprofen a week out.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
